messages:
maria: quick summary — ran the same A100 model (fp16 + int8 quant) across AWS/GCP/Azure to compare latencies and throughput. overall medians are similar but GCP eu-west1 has weird 95th spikes (~2.3x). charts: https://rwd-internal/figures/1764027000-a100-interop.png :chart_with_upwards_trend:
kenji: ugh. can you paste the driver / CUDA combos for each run? :thinking:
maria: test matrix:
```
aws-us-east-1    driver=525.85  cuda=11.8  instance=p4d.24xlarge
gcp-europe-west1 driver=470.57  cuda=11.6  instance=a2-highgpu-1g
azure-uksouth    driver=525.85  cuda=11.8  instance=Standard_ND96asr_v4
```
anita: driver mismatch stands out — GCP still on 470.x in eu-west1. sometimes older drivers fall back to slower cuBLAS/int8 kernels or different batch algo. did you see kernel fallback logs?
maria: yes — saw fallback on many int8 matmul calls on GCP:
```
[WARN] cudnn: fallback to algo 3 for matmul (int8) - heuristics mismatch
[INFO] perf: selected algo=FFT for conv; fallback_count=37
```
oliver: what batch sizes did you test? small-batch tails often explode if kernels aren't using persistent algo or autotuner is disabled.
maria: ran batch=1/4/8. quick numbers (p50 / p95 / throughput requests/s) from the same lib + model: 
```
region            p50   p95   rps (batch8)
aws-us-east-1     38ms  210ms 1200
gcp-europe-west1  46ms  560ms  980
azure-uksouth     39ms  230ms 1150
```
notes: GCP p95 increases mostly for batch1 and batch4; batch8 improved but still worse tail.
kenji: can you repro with probe harness (nsys + perf counters) and a minimal script? also record `nvidia-smi -q` and `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` so infra can check driver packaging.
maria: already ran a light profile. attached command we used:
```
./bench/run_infer.sh --model redwood-v1 --batch 1,4,8 --quant int8,fp16 --profile nsys --iters 200
```
and we captured `nsys` reports per-run.
deploy-bot: FYI infra: kernel/driver rollout in europe-west1 completed yesterday — nodes that didn't restart migrated to 470.57 -> 525.85 on 2026-01-15 03:12:22 UTC.
anita: that explains it — some machines may have mixed driver/CUDA stacks during the window which causes inconsistent kernel dispatch. suggestion: pin to (driver 525.85 + cuda 11.8) for the next run or force deterministic cuBLAS algos when measuring.
oliver: try forcing cublas algo selection and disabling autotune for a repro: e.g. export CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 and set TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=0 (or the equivalent in your runtime) — then rerun a couple of cold-starts. can also test setting `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY` vs `DEFAULT` to see if load ordering helps.
kenji: also try quant sanity check — disable int8 path and compare fp16 only to isolate quant kernel fallbacks.
maria: good plan. I'll run a pinned-driver run in a staging fleet (all nodes forced to 525.85/cuda11.8) and re-run bench with heavy profiling. i'll push raw nsys + perf bundles to the shared folder and post here.
kenji: thanks. if that reproduces we should open an infra ticket to request a coordinated driver update across GCP eu-west1 (no stagger) and add a CI check for driver/CUDA parity.
maria: filing infra ticket with logs + nsys links once done. moving to run now — will report back in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
